plan: 1 Kings 22:10-28; 2 Chronicles 18:9-27; 1 Kings 22:29-35; 2 Chronicles 18:28-34; 1 Kings 22:36-40, 51-53; 2 Chronicles 19:1-11; 2 Chronicles 20:1-30

readings.title: Micaiah's Prophecy of Doom
readings.subtitle: A Lying Spirit Sent from the Throne of Heaven
readings.text: [1 Kings 22:10] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl and Yehoshaphat sovereign of Yehuḏah were sitting, each on his throne, dressed in their robes, at a threshing-floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomeron. And all the prophets were prophesying before them. [11] And Tsiḏqiyah son of Kena‛anah had made horns of iron for himself, and said, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘With these you push <dn>את</dn> the Arameans until they are destroyed.’ ”</dq> [12] And all the prophets were prophesying so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Gil‛aḏ and prosper, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give it into the hand of the sovereign.” [13] And the messenger who had gone to call Miḵayehu spoke to him, saying, “See now, the words of the prophets with one mouth are good towards the sovereign. Please, let your word be like the word of one of them, and you shall speak good.” [14] And Miḵayehu said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, whatever <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> says to me, <dn>את</dn> that <dn>I</dn> speak.” [15] And he came to the sovereign, and the sovereign said to him, “Miḵayehu, do we go against Ramoth Gil‛aḏ to battle, or do we refrain?” And he answered him, “Go and prosper, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give it into the hand of the sovereign!” [16] And the sovereign said to him, “How many times have <dn>I</dn> made you swear that you do not speak to me, except the truth, in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [17] So he said, “<dn>I</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ěl scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>‘These have no master. Let everyone return to his house in peace.’ ”</dq> [18] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said to Yehoshaphat, “Have <dn>I</dn> not said to you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?” [19] Then he said, “Therefore hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: <dn>I</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sitting on <dn>His</dn> throne, and all the host of the heavens standing by <dn>Him</dn>, on <dn>His</dn> right and on <dn>His</dn> left. [20] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>‘Who shall entice <dn>את</dn> Aḥaḇ to go up and fall at Ramoth Gil‛aḏ?’</dq> And this one said this, and another said that. [21] “And a spirit came forward and stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘Let me entice him.’ [22] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>‘In what way?’</dq> And he said, ‘<dn>I</dn> shall go out and be a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>‘Entice him, and also prevail. Go out and do so.’</dq> [23] “And now, see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has put a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken evil concerning you.” [24] And Tsiḏqiyahu son of Kena‛anah came near and struck <dn>את</dn> Miḵayehu on the cheek, and said, “Where did the spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pass over from me to speak to you?” [25] And Miḵayehu said, “Look, you shall see on that day when you go into an inner room to hide!” [26] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said, “Take <dn>את</dn> Miḵayehu, and return him to Amon the governor of the city, and to Yo’ash son of the sovereign, [27] and say, ‘Thus said the sovereign, “Put <dn>את</dn> this one in prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction until <dn>I</dn> come in peace.” ’ ” [28] And Miḵayehu said, “If you ever return in peace, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not spoken by me.” And he said, “Hear, all you people!”

readings.title: The Death of Ahab
readings.subtitle: A Random Arrow Fulfills a Direct Prophecy
readings.text: [1 Kings 22:29] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl and Yehoshaphat the sovereign of Yehuḏah went up to Ramoth Gil‛aḏ. [30] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl said to Yehoshaphat, “Let me disguise myself and go into battle, but you put on your robes.” So the sovereign of Yisra’ěl disguised himself and went into battle. [31] And the sovereign of Aram had commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, “Fight with no one small or great, but only with <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Yisra’ěl.” [32] And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw <dn>את</dn> Yehoshaphat, that they said, “Indeed, it is the sovereign of Yisra’ěl!” So they turned aside to fight against him, and Yehoshaphat cried out. [33] And it came to be, when the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, that they turned back from pursuing him. [34] And a man drew a bow in his simplicity, and struck <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Yisra’ěl between the joints of his armour. And he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for <dn>I</dn> am wounded.” [35] And the battle increased that day. And the sovereign was propped up in his chariot, facing the Arameans, and died at evening, and the blood ran out from the wound onto the floor of the chariot.

readings.title: The Prophecy of Elijah Fulfilled
readings.subtitle: The Dogs Lick Ahab's Blood and Ahaziah Reigns
readings.text: [1 Kings 22:36] And as the sun was going down, a shout passed through the camp, saying, “Each to his city, and each to his land!” [37] So the sovereign died and was brought to Shomeron, and they buried <dn>את</dn> the sovereign in Shomeron. [38] And when <dn>את</dn> the chariot was washed at a pool in Shomeron, the dogs licked up his blood, where the whores bathed, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had spoken. [39] And the rest of the acts of Aḥaḇ and all that he did, and the ivory house which he built and all the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [40] So Aḥaḇ slept with his fathers, and Aḥazyahu his son reigned in his place. [51] Aḥazyahu son of Aḥaḇ began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron in the seventeenth year of Yehoshaphat sovereign of Yehuḏah, and reigned two years over Yisra’ěl, [52] and did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and walked in the way of his father and in the way of his mother and in the way of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin, [53] and served <dn>את</dn> Ba‛al and bowed himself to it, and provoked <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, according to all that his father had done.
